subject: Urgent: AWB missing / label delamination on air consolidated pallet — reconsign plan
messages:
From: Nate Hsu <nate@quickship.co>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Hannah Lowe <hannah@brightlineevents.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Consolidation split — AWB missing on Pallet A

Hi Stephanie / Hannah,

Quick heads up from the field: during consolidation at LAX for the Redwood booth shipment (air consolidated house AWB 123-45678901), our sorter flagged that one pallet (Pallet A) did not have a scannable AWB on the top of the pallet. Manifest has the pallet listed, but label delaminated and fell into the case during handling.

We pulled the manifest and packing reference (attached: manifest_snapshot.pdf) — Pallet A shows in the HAWB but the physical AWB sticker is not readable. That puts the pallet at risk for a customs hold at the first airport of arrival if the AWB cannot be verified.

What we need from Redwood:
- Confirm the HAWB / MAWB mapping you expect for Pallet A (so we can match to your broker records)
- Confirm preferred remediation (relabel onsite vs reconsign to a local courier)

We can attempt to reapply a label onsite if you authorize, but since this is an international consolidation there may be documentation the broker needs. Holding for your instruction.

Thanks,
Nate
QuickShip Operations

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Nate Hsu <nate@quickship.co>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Consolidation split — AWB missing on Pallet A

Nate — thanks for flagging and for the snapshot.

On Wed, Jul 1, 2026 at 9:30 AM Nate Hsu <nate@quickship.co> wrote:
> Quick heads up from the field: during consolidation at LAX for the Redwood booth shipment (air consolidated house AWB 123-45678901), our sorter flagged that one pallet (Pallet A) did not have a scannable AWB on the top of the pallet. Manifest has the pallet listed, but label delaminated and fell into the case during handling.

Confirming next steps from Redwood:
1) Marissa — can you pull the original BOL + packing list for this MAWB and confirm the HAWB <-> Pallet A mapping? Attach to thread.
2) Ben — if QuickShip can reapply a label onsite, please confirm whether they can use the existing MAWB number (preferred) or if they need a reconsignment to a new airway bill. Also confirm insurance/claim implications for a relabeled pallet.
3) Nate — if relabel is not viable, propose reconsign carrier and transit time (we prefer to avoid a customs gate hold).

If customs needs evidence of the original AWB, we can provide BOL + manifest + invoice. Please treat this as time-sensitive — showstaging arrival window is tight.

I’m looping in Marissa and Ben for docs and ops.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen

Stephanie / Ben — I pulled the shipping packet from our S3 archive and attached the BOL: BOL_redwood_0726.pdf.

Quick notes:
- MAWB (master AWB): 123-45678901
- HAWB for Redwood exhibit set: HAWB-REW-0092 maps to Pallet A (two skids: A and B) per packing_list.xlsx (we have the internal SKU grouping there).
- Invoice and commercial docs are in the folder (link in metadata).

If QuickShip can reapply and ensure the MAWB number is visible, that should be sufficient for customs to match the pallet to the MAWB at arrival. If they need the physical label replaced with a new AWB number, we will need to coordinate reconsignment and update the broker (this will add ~24–48 hrs).

I’ve attached BOL_redwood_0726.pdf (see attachments).

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Consolidation split — AWB missing on Pallet A

Thanks — I just spoke with Nate on the line. QuickShip located the AWB underside and confirmed the printed sticker delaminated; the number is still in their system but not scannable on the pallet surface. Nate will: 
- Reapply a new label with the existing MAWB 123-45678901 and sign the handler acknowledgment
- Send photo proof after label application (attached: tracking_snapshot.png)
- If Customs at the destination requires, QuickShip will produce an administrative reconsign and we will coordinate a rebook (reconsign_order.pdf stub attached).

Operational ask for Redwood: please confirm whether we should authorize QuickShip to reapply the MAWB label onsite (fastest) or insist on a new AWB (slower). My recommendation: authorize relabel on-site with photo proof + BOL confirmation — keeps us within the show delivery window.

Ben Carter

- Relabel applied with MAWB 123-45678901 (photo attached)
